newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai rice ends down in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai rice ends down in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai rice futures ended down in slow trading on Friday, with investors withdrawing their money on dull sentiment, traders said.
The key October 1996 contract ended at 2,290 yuan ($275) per tonne, down 12 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 2,300 and hit a low of 2,285.
Combined volume fell to 1,700 tonnes from 1,900.
Traders said that investors continued to shift their money into other markets with the end of the September contract, in which most investors suffered heavy losses.
"The more active Shanghai stock market attracted many individuals away from the rice market," one trader said.
Shanghai's A share market rose sharply on Friday with an inflow of hot money.
Traders said rice was likely to remain steady in the next few days with a lack of market-moving news.
